About the lab

Senior research in Astro Lab

Students develop a research question from the literature, carry out a group project, and present their work at tjSTAR.

Current Research Class links and journal club

Reading and discussion

Class generally begins with astronomy news of the day and discussion of recent papers, or with journal club, where students review the papers they have been reading. These conversations help students become familiar with the research literature.

From literature to a proposal

Once students are sufficiently familiar with the literature, they form groups and brainstorm project ideas. Each group writes a formal research proposal in LaTeX. After the proposal is approved, students continue researching their topic and carrying out the project.

A daily research record

Throughout the year, each student keeps a daily journal of the work they are doing and the papers they are reading. The journal provides a continuing record of their research.

Presenting the work at tjSTAR

The year culminates in tjSTAR. Students prepare a portfolio that includes a research paper and a poster. They defend their work in a poster session and give a talk.

For prospective students

Preparing for senior research

Junior students interested in senior research in Astro Lab are encouraged to build their astronomy background through TJ's Advanced Astronomy electives. The electives support later research work with shared scientific context, quantitative methods, and astronomical problem solving.

Research modes

Methods used in the lab

  • Observational astronomy and calibrated measurement
  • Public survey catalogs, images, spectra, and time series
  • Numerical models and computational astrophysics
  • Instrumentation, automation, and data-quality methods
